turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry we're a bit late, doctor. The bus from Rathmines was desperate, and then the rain started.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): In you come. What's the problem?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I have a blocked nose, pressure across my face, and the discharge has turned green. It has been two weeks... err, forgive me, ten days.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Both sides?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Mainly the right side, doctor.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any fever?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor. I did check it before we left, and it was 37.2.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sore throat?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No, doctor.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Double vision, or swelling about the eye?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Neither. My sight is as usual.
[SEG0014] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's very tired though. And he sleeps badly, up and down all night.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): The tiredness is correct, I am afraid. This is the second week of it. But I do not sleep badly. My sleep is much as usual.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nasal spray?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, every day. I thought the name was Beconase, but err, it is Flixonase, umm, fluticasone, two sprays in each nostril once a day.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any tablets?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): Cetrizine, ten milligrams at night, for the hay fever. I have been on it for years.
[SEG0020] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He does not take the tablets on Sundays. I set them out, and the Sunday one is still in the box.
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): Forgive me, that is not quite right. It is Saturdays I miss, not Sundays. The other evenings I take it.
[SEG0022] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Ah, Saturdays. I had the wrong day.
[SEG0023] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His sister is on metformin for her diabetes. That's hers, not his. I only mention it in case it runs in the family.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not his. Hay fever we know. Sister with diabetes, noted. Any cuts slow to heal?
[SEG0025] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He nicked his finger chopping onions, and it healed in five days. Ordinary enough.
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes, that is correct. It healed within five days.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): No. I have never smoked.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. Tender over the right cheek. Lining of the nose is swollen, green mucus on the right, throat clear, no swelling of the face.
[SEG0030] person_4 (NURSE): Uh, sorry. Vitals from outside. Temperature 37.2, same as he told me, pulse 74, blood pressure 130 over 82, oxygen 98 percent.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any drug allergies?
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): None, doctor.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): This is sinusitis after the cold. Most of these settle without an antibiotic.

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll book bloods for Thursday morning, half eight. Full blood count and CRP. No fasting. Take your usual tablets that morning. If those are borderline we do a CT of the sinuses. If they're not, we don't.

[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): I'll see you in two weeks. If it has not settled in five days, or you get a fever or the eye swells, we start amoxicillin, five hundred milligrams three times a day for five days. Not before.
[SEG0036] person_3 (PATIENT): Thank you. Should I carry on with the spray, doctor?
[SEG0037] person_2 (DOCTOR): Keep the Flixonase. Saline rinses if you like. Paracetamol, one gram up to four times a day, for the pressure. No decongestant spray.
[SEG0038] person_1 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We'll be grand for Thursday if the parking isn't as bad as last time. We were circling for ages.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Reception will book the bloods and the review. Mind how you go.

spec.situation: Blocked nose, facial pressure and green discharge ten days after a cold; second week of tiredness; uses nasal spray daily; doctor explains most settle without antibiotics, gives a back-up plan.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
